etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Latin dubius; like doubt, from Latin duo (cognate to English two), implying “two alternatives” (yes or no, true or false, etc.).
senses: (of a statement, matter, thing, or person) Arousing doubt; questionable; open to suspicion.
(of a person) In disbelief; wavering, uncertain, or hesitating in opinion; inclined to doubt; undecided.
